notes.claim: Percentage change is the change written as a fraction of the original amount and converted to a percentage.
A percentage change can be either an increase or a decrease.
Percentage points are used when comparing two percentages: a rate going from 10% to 12% has increased by 2 percentage points.

sources.title: Percentage change - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Percentage change is calculated by writing the actual change as a fraction of the original amount, and converting to a percentage.

sources.title: Percentage Change - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Percentage change is the amount that a quantity has changed, expressed as a percentage of the original value. This can be either an increase or a decrease.

sources.title: Beginners:Statistical concept - Percentage change and percentage points - Statistics Explained - Eurostat
sources.quote: The term percentage points is used when comparing two different percentages.

sources.title: Glossary:Percentage point Statistics Explained — Eurostat
sources.quote: Example: A rate was 10% and it increased to 12%, then it increased by 2 percentage points.
